options.note: A NAT gateway gives private IPv4 addresses outbound internet access and does not accept connections initiated from the internet.

options.text: Assign public IPv4 addresses to the servers and route 0.0.0.0/0 from their subnets to the internet gateway.
options.note: This makes the servers reachable from the internet over IPv4, relying only on security groups, which violates the policy.

explanation: For outbound-only internet access, use a NAT gateway for IPv4 and an egress-only internet gateway for IPv6. IPv6 addresses need no translation, so the egress-only internet gateway provides the one-way behavior that NAT provides for IPv4.

text:
A company processes sensitive data on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The VPC has no internet gateway or NAT gateway, and the instances access Amazon S3 through a gateway VPC endpoint. All of the company's buckets belong to accounts in its organization in AWS Organizations. The security team must prevent data from being copied from the instances to any S3 bucket outside the organization, even if someone on an instance uses access keys from an AWS account that is not in the organization.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach a service control policy (SCP) that denies S3 actions unless the aws:ResourceOrgID condition key matches the company's organization ID.
options.note: SCPs apply only to principals in the organization's accounts. Access keys from an outside account are not governed by the SCP, so data could still be copied to an outside bucket.

options.text: Attach an endpoint policy to the gateway VPC endpoint that allows S3 actions only when the aws:ResourceOrgID condition key matches the company's organization ID.
options.note: Every S3 request from the VPC goes through the endpoint, whatever credentials are used. The endpoint policy denies requests to buckets owned outside the organization.

options.text: Add an outbound rule to the instances' security group that allows HTTPS only to the AWS managed prefix list for Amazon S3.
options.note: The S3 prefix list covers every bucket in the Region, including other companies' buckets, so it cannot distinguish the organization's buckets from outside ones.

options.text: Add a bucket policy to every company bucket that denies requests that do not come through the gateway VPC endpoint.
options.note: This protects the company's own buckets from outside access. It does nothing to stop the instances from writing to buckets that the company does not own.

explanation: A VPC endpoint policy controls which resources can be reached through the endpoint, regardless of the caller's credentials, which makes it the network perimeter control against data exfiltration. Bucket policies protect your own buckets, and SCPs control only your own principals. Data perimeters combine all three.

text:
A company has 60 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations, and new accounts are created every month. The central security team requires that every Application Load Balancer and every Amazon API Gateway stage in every account, including resources created in the future, be protected by a baseline set of AWS WAF rules. Application teams must be able to add their own rules on top of the baseline.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy a web ACL with the baseline rules to every account and Region. Ask application teams to associate the web ACL with their resources.
options.note: StackSets can create the web ACL everywhere, but association depends on each team, so new resources can go unprotected. Nothing enforces the baseline.

options.text: Enable AWS Security Hub CSPM in all accounts and use its controls to report ALBs and API Gateway stages that have no web ACL. Have the security team remediate findings.
options.note: Security Hub CSPM detects unprotected resources, but remediation is manual and protection is not applied automatically to new resources.

options.text: Use an AWS Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy with the baseline rule groups, scoped to the organization, with auto remediation for ALBs and API Gateway stages.
options.note: Firewall Manager centrally applies WAF policies across the organization, including new accounts and resources, and lets account owners add their own rules between the first and last rule groups.

options.text: Subscribe every account to AWS Shield Advanced and turn on automatic application layer DDoS mitigation for all ALBs and API Gateway stages.
options.note: Shield Advanced focuses on DDoS protection, and its automatic mitigation creates rules only in response to attacks. It does not apply the company's baseline rule set.

explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is the service for centrally enforcing AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, security group, and Network Firewall policies across an organization, automatically covering new accounts and resources. StackSets and Security Hub CSPM can deploy or detect, but they do not enforce protection continuously.

text:
An ecommerce company serves its website through Amazon CloudFront. Competitors use automated scrapers to harvest product prices. The scrapers rotate IP addresses and keep their request rate per IP address low. The company wants to block or challenge common bots and scrapers while continuing to allow verified search engine crawlers that are important for its search ranking.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Add an AWS WAF rate-based rule to a web ACL on the CloudFront distribution that blocks IP addresses that send more than 100 requests in 5 minutes.
options.note: Rate-based rules catch high-volume clients. These scrapers rotate IP addresses and stay under per-IP limits, and the rule cannot tell verified search engine crawlers from other bots.

options.text: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and add the CloudFront distribution as a protected resource.
options.note: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks. Low-rate scraping is not a DDoS attack, and Shield Advanced does not classify bots.

options.text: Deploy a Lambda@Edge function on viewer requests that inspects the User-Agent header and blocks requests from known scraper user agents.
options.note: This is custom code that must be maintained, and scrapers can easily set a browser or search engine User-Agent to evade it.

options.text: Add the AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group to the distribution's web ACL, and configure it to block or challenge unverified bots.
options.note: Bot Control is an AWS managed rule group that identifies bots, distinguishes verified bots such as search engine crawlers, and can block or challenge the rest, with no code to maintain.

explanation: The AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group classifies bot traffic and verifies legitimate bots such as search engines, so it can block scrapers that stay under rate limits. Rate-based rules address volume per IP, and Shield addresses DDoS.

text:
A company lets customers upload documents to an Amazon S3 bucket by using presigned URLs. Before a downstream workflow processes a document, every newly uploaded object must be scanned for malware, and the scan result must be recorded on the object. The company does not want to manage servers or maintain antivirus signature updates.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 on the bucket with result tagging turned on. Start the downstream workflow from its scan result events in EventBridge.
options.note: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 scans new objects automatically with AWS-managed detection, can tag each object with its scan result, and publishes results to EventBridge to trigger the next step.

options.text: Enable GuardDuty S3 Protection for the account. Start the downstream workflow from the GuardDuty findings in Amazon EventBridge that reference the bucket.
options.note: S3 Protection analyzes S3 data events in CloudTrail for suspicious access, such as requests from known malicious IP addresses. It does not scan object contents for malware.

options.text: Have EC2 workers download each new object, then run GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 on-demand scans of the workers' EBS volumes and tag the object.
options.note: On-demand scans target an EC2 instance's EBS volumes, at most once per hour per instance, not individual S3 objects. The company would also manage the workers, which it wants to avoid.

options.text: Send S3 event notifications to an Amazon SQS queue that an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances processes with open source antivirus software that tags each object.
options.note: This can scan and tag objects, but the company must manage the instances and keep the antivirus signatures up to date, which it wants to avoid.

explanation: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 is a fully managed scanner for newly uploaded objects, with optional result tagging and EventBridge events for downstream automation. Do not confuse it with GuardDuty S3 Protection, which watches access patterns, or Malware Protection for EC2, which scans EBS volumes.
